highlights.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as firm reports bumper results
highlights.summary: The AI chip giant reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday after the dramatic exit of Jensen Huang.
body: Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it has no plans to reinstate ousted co-founder Jensen Huang.
In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Colette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this."
The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping by 4.8% in after-hours trading.
Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China.

highlights.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
highlights.summary: Supported by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, scholars are exploring how AI is impacting the human experience and reshaping higher education.
body: MIT students are going to office hours less often. They’re spending less time working through problem sets, and with one another. Those were among the findings of MIT’s recent report on artificial intelligence and education, and they are one reason a growing number of MIT faculty are concerned about how generative AI is both changing how people work and affecting how they think, learn, and relate to one another.

For the MIT Human Insight Collaborative (MITHIC), those questions have become a central focus, and MITHIC is working with collaborators across the Institute, including the Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing (SERC), to help MIT address them.

Launched in 2024 as a strategic initiative, MITHIC brings together scholars, artists, educators, and researchers to explore the human dimensions of the defining challenges of our time. Since its launch, MITHIC has supported 67 projects across 31 MIT units, offering a total of $5.5 million in funding.
Roughly a third of those projects are focused on AI, society, and humanity — a topic that MITHIC faculty co-lead Heather Paxson says has become an increasingly important part of the initiative.

highlights.title: Belief and bench help Northern Ireland scale new heights as promotion secured
highlights.summary: Manager Michael O'Neill hails the belief shown by his side after they come from behind against Hungary to earn the draw required for promotion to Nations League A.
body: After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Puskas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit - on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game - displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point from a 1-1 draw in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.

highlights.title: GTA 6's Release Will Stress The Internet Just As Everything's Falling Apart
highlights.summary: In early November, some internet service providers warned their customers that pre-downloads of Grand Theft Auto 6 were causing network slowdown issues for everyone on the service. That problem became visible before millions of gamers tried to log into the same game simultaneously.
body: If you've ever been around for the release of a big new game, you know that day-one network issues are fairly common. Some hiccups are worse than others, of course, but most people are probably already bracing for some potential hitches when we're talking about the biggest game launch of all time. What makes GTA 6 different from other game releases is its scale and timing.

The highly anticipated sequel first began causing issues for some ISPs when Rockstar opened preloads for the 212 GB game on Nov. 10. At the time, some providers claimed that the game was directly responsible for never-before-seen traffic peaks so high that they congested the proverbial internet tubes for everyone else.

Rockstar undoubtedly foresaw that the problem could occur or worsen by launch day. The studio dropped a couple of patches in a staggered rollout prior to launch. The release cadence made it less likely that GTA 6 fans could overload Rockstar's, PlayStation's, and Xbox's servers at the same time. Service providers have also been gearing up for Nov. 19, with at least one ISP advertising that it would offer increased download speeds specifically for GTA 6.

highlights.title: ‘The Predators Are Real’: Senate Hearing Slams Roblox Over Child Sex Abuse
highlights.summary: US Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin have introduced legislation to make it easier for families to sue if their child has been harmed through the massive gaming platform.
body: People who say they were groomed on Roblox testified in front of a Congressional subcommittee Tuesday about safety risks associated with the popular gaming platform frequented by kids and teenagers.

“Roblox is one of the most popular gaming platforms in the world,” Republican senator Josh Hawley said in his opening remarks. “If your children are on Roblox they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators … to sexually exploitative content, left, right, and center.”

The process of forced arbitration “strips consumers and workers of their rights,” testified Myriam Gilles, a law professor at Northwestern University who is an expert on forced arbitration. “I never expected to come before this body to talk about its use against 9-year-olds, but that’s where we are.”

Roblox is currently facing nearly 200 lawsuits from families who allege that their children were groomed by sexual predators posing as children on the platform. According to Hawley, Roblox CEO David Baszucki was invited to testify at the hearing but declined.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
highlights.summary: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
body: Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.
But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

body: Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for O’Neill’s young outfit, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland’s one-point advantage as group leaders. As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation – with Rajmund Toth firing over late on – but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of their campaign.

“It’s a great feeling for us,” said O’Neill, who had to watch the game from the stands as he served a touchline ban. “We set out when we came into this level of the competition to first of all try and stay and we knew to be in the top two positions would help us.

body: Embark Studios is facing backlash after a now-deleted video was uploaded to The Finals' official social media accounts recapping highlights from The Grand Major’s APAC Closed Qualifiers. The audio commentary that played over the video is at the center of this blowback, as the casters who originally commentated these matches were replaced by the game's fictional AI commentators, Scotty and June. While this video has since been removed from public viewing, remarks from casters in the community paint a grim picture of what they saw.

“After four cycles, open/closed [qualifiers], the time, effort, passion, and emotion myself, @TheeHyperactive, and @bluepanda_casts put in, we get replaced by two AI casters who even quote us. I get they are a part of the game, but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals,” commentator Proto / Kai wrote in a viral post on Twitter/X.

highlights.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
highlights.summary: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking…
body: The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

highlights.title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
highlights.summary: Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as "Tasks" and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.
body: Tasks in Gemini allows the AI agent to call businesses on your behalf, purchase items with Google Pay, and more.

Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager. US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.

Tasks in Gemini is just one of the many agentic AI features that have emerged over the past year, including Claude Duet, OpenAI’s Dots, and Meta’s Muse. Google says Gemini will perform tasks in a “hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.” You can also provide instructions for Gemini while it completes tasks. When performing more sensitive tasks, like purchasing an item, it will stop working and ask for your permission before following through.
Sign in to see your notifications or create an account to join the conversation.

highlights.title: Republic of Ireland talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals
highlights.summary: Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott reflects on a transformative 12 months for both club and country after scoring a double in the win against Kosovo.
body: A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.

His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.
The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.
Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat
highlights.summary: England’s exam regulator says those caught using AI or smart glasses face disqualification from GCSEs and A-levels. Students in England could suffer “life-altering” penalties if they are caught relying on AI or smart glasses to cheat, England’s qualifications regulator has said.
body: The head of Ofqual, Ian Bauckham, said students could be disqualified from GCSEs, A-levels and other qualifications if they tried to use AI in assessed coursework, and called for retailers to be barred from marketing wearable technology for exam cheating.

“If you are caught committing malpractice with an important, high-stakes qualification … in extreme cases you can lose the entire qualification which, as I am sure you can imagine, can be life-altering for somebody’s future,” Bauckham told the Press Association.

As coursework submission deadlines near, Ofqual is launching a publicity campaign to make it clear to students that using AI for assessments such as extended essays and failing to declare it will not be tolerated.

Bauckham is also writing to examination boards in England to tell them that exam hall invigilators and supervisors should be trained to spot the “emerging risk” posed by wearable devices during next summer’s exam season.

highlights.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
highlights.summary: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.
body: Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.

On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

“We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”

highlights.title: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers recount their terrifying experiences of sleep paralysis in response to an article by Amy Fleming. I experienced sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations from childhood and into adulthood, with the episodes only waning in my 30s ( Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep…
body: I experienced hallucinations in the form of severe perspective distortion (oversized bed and rooms) and full hallucinations/dream states, auditory hallucinations (screaming and loud thumping) and, of course, paralysis. I didn’t know at what point I was asleep or if I had woken and could easily slip back into a hypnagogic state. I only became aware of this state as an adult, having been referred to a psychiatrist on an unrelated matter.

Some of the episodes were literally the stuff of nightmares. I have always had exceptionally vivid dreams and rarely do I go through a night without a dream waking me up (or so it seems). Once I understood what was happening, it was less terrifying and more fascinating, though the actual physical state cannot fail to be frightening.

Sleep paralysis struck me years before I learned, at an exhibition at the Wellcome Institute, that this was not just me being weird in my sleep, but a proper thing with a name. And yes, it is absolutely petrifying. I still remember how relieved I was on the one hand and fascinated on the other by all the evidence of sleep paralysis through the centuries at this exhibition.

highlights.summary: Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, but Nigeria are in trouble, and struggling Tunisia fail with an impassioned penalty protest.
body: Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations before Cameroon and Morocco were among five others to join them with two games to spare - but there was penalty drama in Tripoli.
Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of Afcon, are at risk of missing out after a contentious 1-1 draw against Libya.
Libya's penalty equaliser just before half-time followed protest scenes lasting over five minutes as players and staff from the Carthage Eagles challenged the decision.

The video assistant referee system is not used in Afcon qualifying, and Tunisia's remonstrating with the fourth official on the touchline ultimately only served to delay the spot-kick, which Ezoo El Mariamy, the player who was adjudged to have been fouled, converted.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

The project featured the hit single “E85” that reached No. 3 on Billboard’s Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart and No. 15 on the Hot 100. The Houston rapper spent much of the year on the road as part of his “Octane World Tour,” which had a first run of arena shows from May to July before picking back up for a “Nitrous: New World Tour” addendum to the trek from August through the end of November, when he’ll wrap the shows at London’s O2 Arena.

Yesterday, Toliver made waves with a substantial five nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards. In addition to best new artist, Toliver was nominated for best rap album with “Octane”; best rap performance with “Body”; and best rap song and best melodic rap performance with “E85.”

body: Apparently, the secret to a stress-free Christmas involves roasting a kilogram of chicken wings and simmering stock for hours, making marmalade from scratch, infusing gin with Sichuan peppercorns and, should we have a spare afternoon, heading into the woods to forage for Douglas fir needles. I had naively imagined that time-saving tips might actually save time.
Instead, we are encouraged to embark on an elaborate programme of culinary projects, requiring specialist ingredients, considerable effort and a seemingly inexhaustible supply of enthusiasm.

Every year we have a Christmas dinner that is cooked in advance and frozen. In our house that is usually chilli con carne, but we have done curries and other dishes. The main aim is to be able to do the bulk of the cooking on a weekend in late November or early December.

highlights.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
highlights.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he's AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it.
body: But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”

body: Linares is being held at the El Paso Processing Center, according to federal detention records reviewed by the San Antonio Express-News. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said he was arrested at El Paso International Airport on Sunday after overstaying the period he was authorized to remain in the country.
The 41-year-old boxing great, who captured titles across three weight classes from featherweight to lightweight, first disclosed his detention in a post on X on Sunday.
“ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy,” Linares wrote in Spanish. He has not posted publicly since.

ICE spokeswoman Leticia Zamarripa said Linares was arrested by US Border Patrol agents and ICE officers on 15 November after entering the United States on 26 October 2023 with permission to remain for a temporary period.
